Loopback REST daemon (default :8420) consumed by the Obsidian companion plugin.

R06 concurrency model (ARCH §3, §8): the global ``guard`` mutex is gone.
One writer connection is serialized by ``write_lock`` (SQLite WAL admits a
single writer); every reader thread owns a private WAL connection plus a
private warmed router (R01 "one-instance-per-thread" rule), so queries
never block on syncs. Readers pin the active ``filing`` projection
generation and rebuild their warmed views when the writer publishes a new
one (generation-swapped reads); freshness is reported honestly instead of
the hardcoded R00 trusted/organized state.

classes.name: DossierRequest
classes.doc:
R07 additive: compile a query-generated evidence dossier.

Read-only over the generation-pinned reader stack; touches none of the
R06 writer/generation/freshness logic bodies.

classes.name: ReaderView
classes.doc: Thread-private read stack: own WAL connection + warmed router.

classes.name: ServedRuntime
classes.doc:
Process-wide S4 serving state for one app (S6 cutover).

Holds the shared :class:`ServedVectors` snapshot plus a SINGLE
background maintenance thread (seed / catch-up jobs, coalesced).
G1 immutable serving: maintenance NEVER mutates the published
snapshot — it builds a thread-private clone and publishes with one
atomic pointer swap under ``lock``. Request paths read the pointer
under the same momentary lock and retain that immutable snapshot for
the whole request, so queries serve continuously during maintenance
and NEVER detach for it. The worker thread is a daemon: a stuck build
can delay, never hang, shutdown (the join is bounded).

functions.name: start_maintenance_worker
functions.doc:
Start the supervised background worker (idempotent; S3 wiring + G1).

The worker owns a private WAL handle on the same file and drains the
shared outbox outside every writer transaction, so stalled semantic
work never blocks lexical retrieval. G1: write paths never drain, so
this worker is the sole projection driver (auto-started under
persistent serving).

functions.name: stop_maintenance_worker
functions.doc: Stop the background worker and close its private handle (S3 wiring only).

functions.name: _cap_request_threads
functions.doc: Cap the anyio worker-thread pool (bounds reader retention).

functions.name: _is_busy_error
functions.doc: True for transient SQLite lock contention (SQLITE_BUSY / locked).

functions.name: _busy_503
functions.doc: Contention exhaustion: retryable 503, never a 500.

functions.name: _retry_write
functions.doc:
Run idempotent write ``fn`` with bounded busy retry.

Rolls back before each retry (a busy commit can leave the txn open);
re-raises the last busy error when attempts exhaust (callers convert
to 503). Non-busy errors propagate immediately. Only idempotent
sections may use this (publish/retract/facet-ensure/generation
publish); the non-idempotent facet fold-out relies on the worker's
sub-second holds fitting inside the 5 s busy_timeout instead.

functions.name: served_status_block
functions.doc:
Additive ``/api/status`` served-persistent block (S6, gated).

Reports the open-only snapshot state, background seed/catch-up
receipts, the disk-budget verdict (old/new generations + WAL), and
the measured queue lag against its bound. Read-only: never starts
maintenance, never waits on it.

functions.name: served_after_write
functions.doc:
Post-commit hook: schedule background served catch-up (S6, gated).

Non-blocking and exception-free: writers only enqueue a coalesced job;
all encoding/publication happens on the single maintenance thread, so
write latency never includes vector work and freshness never awaits it.
No-op unless persistent serving was enabled at startup.

functions.name: check_disk_budget
functions.doc:
Old/new generations + WAL against the disk budget (S6 envelope check).

``served`` (a :class:`ServedVectors`, when a base is open) contributes
the per-generation accounting; DB/WAL bytes are always measured from
``db_path``. Passes iff the footprint fits ``budget_bytes`` (when set)
AND host headroom covers ``min_headroom_ratio`` × footprint.

functions.name: filing_watermark
functions.doc: Lexical watermark: live atom count + max rowid (monotonic-ish).

functions.name: publish_filing_generation
functions.doc:
Publish a new ``filing`` generation row covering the writer's commit.

Writers call this with ``commit=False`` INSIDE their data transaction so
the generation row commits atomically with the data it describes (ARCH
§3): no snapshot ever contains data without its generation, so the
generation-swap retry in :func:`route_pinned` is sound. Uses the R01
generation helpers unchanged (no R01 semantic change): create-then-
activate is atomic per helper; readers compare the pinned id against the
active row to decide when to swap warmed views.

Standalone calls (``commit=True``) retry transient busy with rollback
(G2 cycle 2); a rolled-back generation id never escapes, so retries
are side-effect free. ``commit=False`` never retries (the caller owns
the txn and any half-written row).

functions.name: _live_centroids
functions.doc: Live facet blobs unpacked (read-only; ghosts never repaired here).

functions.name: _warm_reader_private
functions.doc:
Per-thread private warm: the exact pre-R3 read-only reader warm.

``CascadeRouter.warm()`` issues ``UPDATE``/``COMMIT`` statements
(stale-centroid clearing, per-facet ``refresh_centroid`` for NULL-blob
facets). On a reader those writes contend with the writer's
``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` transactions and stall on ``busy_timeout`` for
seconds — the exact queue-behind-sync the packet forbids. The writer
already maintains every blob incrementally (``assign_facets``/
``detach_atom`` persist per edit, ``clear_stale_centroids`` runs after
every batch), so readers only need live blobs plus the warmed dense
matrix + shared beam view (``FlatHybrid.warm`` is read-only: SELECTs +
numpy). Runs when the shared pool is disabled or has no generation.

functions.name: _attach_pooled
functions.doc:
Attach a pooled view by reference (zero encodes, zero copies).

The dense arrays are attached read-only (numpy reads are thread-safe
and the pooled objects are never mutated in place); centroid vectors
are cheaply copied per reader so the pooled dict stays immutable.

functions.name: shared_warm_status
functions.doc: Additive ``/api/status`` R3 pool block (read-only telemetry).

functions.name: _warm_reader
functions.doc:
Read-only reader warm (C6-3 + R3 pooled generation view).

R3: exactly ONE immutable warmed view exists per generation,
published under ``state.shared_lock`` by a single rebuilder; every
reader attaches it by reference instead of re-encoding the corpus
(pre-R3 each thread paid a full GIL-bound re-encode on first touch,
serializing N threads into an N× storm that starved serving). The
pooled view is built by the same ``FlatHybrid.warm()`` code, so
vectors are bit-identical to a private warm; the rebuilder publishes
only when the generation it built for is still active, and the pool
advances by pointer swap while in-flight readers retain their pinned
snapshot — synchronous visibility invalidation is preserved (a stale
reader is detected by generation mismatch in :func:`get_reader` and
re-attaches, never served stale-as-complete).

functions.name: _build_reader
functions.doc:
Open a private WAL read stack and warm it (caller owns lifecycle).

The open replays idempotent DDL, which takes the write lock briefly
and can race worker holds: bounded busy retry with handle cleanup,
then a retryable 503 (G2 cycle 2; never a 500 for contention). The
warm itself is read-only, so retries only replay a cheap open.

functions.name: _refresh_reader
functions.doc:
In-place generation swap: re-warm the existing stack, keep its connection.

A full rebuild (new connection + full DDL replay + re-warm) costs 2-3x a
re-warm and, under threaded load, lands queries in long tails. Reuse is
snapshot-sound: every statement reads the latest committed state, so
clearing the facet/centroid caches and re-running the read-only warm
yields exactly the post-publication view a fresh connection would build —
with no DDL replay and no connection churn. Falls back to a full rebuild
when the connection is unusable.

functions.name: get_reader
functions.doc:
Thread-local reader; refreshes (generation swap) when stale.

Each thread reuses its own warmed stack across requests. When the
writer has published a newer ``filing`` generation, the stack is
refreshed in place and re-pinned so queries always read a coherent
snapshot at a known generation — never a half-published index.

functions.name: drop_reader
functions.doc: Discard a thread-local reader stack (forces rebuild on next use).

functions.name: _ensure_served_vector
functions.doc:
Pin the served R03 ANN view to the reader's filing generation.

Read-only: rebuilds the thread-local router's in-memory VectorIndex/IVF
from its own snapshot when the serving generation moved, and enables
holon-guided expansion. An unavailable branch (empty/oversize corpus,
build failure) detaches quietly so the named lexical fallbacks serve —
never an error on the query path.

functions.name: _ensure_served_persistent_view
functions.doc:
Pin the S4 persistent view on the reader (S6 cutover, gated).

Drop-in replacement for :func:`_ensure_served_vector` when persistent
serving is enabled: attaches the published base + bounded delta through
the existing ANN branch (INT-2 filtering semantics reused unchanged).
G1 non-blocking contract: the active snapshot pointer is read under a
momentary lock (< 1ms) and the retained IMMUTABLE snapshot serves the
whole request — maintenance NEVER detaches the branch and a busy lock
NEVER detaches it either (the last published snapshot still serves).
Only a genuinely absent/unservable base detaches with an honest note
(legitimate cold-start fallback; first query never triggers a build).

functions.name: route_pinned
functions.doc:
Route a query with generation-swap retry (ARCH §3).

A reader warmed at generation G can race a writer publishing G+1: an
atom id resolved from the warmed dense view may be gone from the live
table (Tier-3 fusion fill ``KeyError``). When — and only when — a newer
active generation explains the miss, the stale stack is dropped and the
query retries on the fresh generation. A miss with no publication
behind it is re-raised: it is a real bug, not a race. Bounded fixture
bound: 4 attempts, then an honest 503 (never stale-as-complete).

Served retrieval (INT-2): the pinned reader also carries the R03 ANN
branch (generation-pinned VectorIndex/IVF with honest route labels) and
holon-guided expansion; the beam/hybrid/lexical branches stay available
as named fallbacks. S6 cutover: when ``state.served_rt`` is set
(``TRACE_LITE_SERVED_PERSISTENT=1`` at startup) the branch is pinned
from the S4 published base + bounded delta via
:func:`_ensure_served_persistent_view` (never a query-path build);
otherwise the legacy query-triggered build runs unchanged.

functions.name: writer
functions.doc: Serialize writer-connection use. Readers never enter here.

functions.name: _prepare_note
functions.doc:
Parse a note + ensure its facets (autocommit phase, no atom writes).

Facet creation commits early (additive, never deletes — always safe) and
therefore must run OUTSIDE any caller-held write transaction. Returns the
parsed note, facet ids, body, and raw payload for the INT-1 write
path (R01 revision + facet mapping + projection drain). Per-note
pre-write snapshots (prior atoms/facets/revision) are taken by
:func:`_snapshot_doc` immediately before each publish.

functions.name: _snapshot_doc
functions.doc:
Pre-write snapshot: prior atom ids, their facets, current revision id,
and per-facet prior member texts for incremental fold-out.

Taken BEFORE ``source_service.publish``/``retract`` deletes the old atom
rows, so facet accumulators can fold the removed members out exactly and
dependent syntheses invalidated afterwards (dependency rows carry no FK
and survive the atom delete; membership rows cascade).

functions.name: _repair_facet_state
functions.doc:
Fold removed members out of facet accumulators (G1 incremental path).

``source_service.publish``/``retract`` removes superseded atom rows in
its own writer transaction (with correct FTS deletes). Each affected
facet folds exactly its removed member texts out of the running sum
(O(removed × dim), no member re-scan on warm accumulators); a cold facet
seeds once from post-delete truth and a stale fold falls back to one
exact reseed inside ``remove_members``. Always persists, including the
emptied-facet NULL branch.

functions.name: _invalidate_for_edit
functions.doc:
Mark dependent syntheses stale after a premise edit/delete (R06-F4).

Requires cover the superseded revision (reaches prior extraction runs
and their anchored assertions transitively) plus every removed atom id
(reaches member-linked holons through surviving dependency rows). The
pipeline-maintained corpus holon is excluded: its state was already
refreshed synchronously by grouping, so it needs no repair. Non-holon
derived rows are traversed but carry no status to flip.

functions.name: ingest_note
functions.doc:
Idempotent single-note upsert with a decoupled fast ACK. Returns atom id.

Per-note flow, all under the caller's ``write_lock`` (R06 writer
serialization stays untouched):

1. parse + ensure facets (autocommit, additive);
2. snapshot prior atoms/facets/revision (+ member texts for fold-out);
3. R01 ``source_service.publish``: one writer transaction inserting the
   immutable revision + lexical delta (atom/FTS) + event + durable
   outbox job. Same key + payload replays return the prior revision
   with NO new job and NO duplicated projections;
4. incremental facet fold-out for removed members + facet mapping of the
   new atom (legacy query behavior preserved: same hints, same
   memberships);
5. premise-edit invalidation (R06 ``invalidate_dependents``; corpus
   excluded) + one ``filing`` generation publish: visibility
   invalidation is synchronous (superseded content is immediately
   invisible), while semantic projection drains asynchronously on the
   background worker (generation-swap retry stays sound).

G1: the write path NEVER drains the projection outbox. Semantic
coverage converges on the worker; freshness reports honest pending
until it does. ``publish`` controls the ``filing`` generation bump.
Replays skip the bump (nothing changed).

functions.name: remove_note
functions.doc:
Retract a note: R01 revision history retained, lexical rows removed.

Same pipeline shape as :func:`ingest_note`: snapshot, R01 ``retract``
(atoms + FTS removed, current pointer nulled, retract job enqueued),
incremental facet fold-out, dependent-synthesis invalidation over the
removed atoms, one ``filing`` generation publish. Retraction is
immediately visible (live rows + generation swap); the retract job
drains asynchronously. Returns atoms removed (0 when the note is
absent, matching legacy behavior).

functions.name: sync_notes
functions.doc:
Sync an explicit list of vault files (used by the background watcher).

INT-1 per-source transaction contract (explicit per ARCH §3: batches
choose all-or-per-source; this path chooses per-source): each note runs
the :func:`ingest_note` pipeline stages 1–5 (parse, R01 publish with
idempotent replay for unchanged files, facet fold-out + mapping, legacy
event), then the batch shares ONE batched invalidation and a SINGLE
``filing`` generation publish — so readers rebuild once per sync and
the generation-swap retry in :func:`route_pinned` stays sound. G1: no
synchronous drain; projection jobs queue durably for the background
worker. Unreadable files are skipped; any other error propagates after
earlier notes committed (per-source, never a half-replaced single
note). No-op batches (nothing synced) publish nothing. Returns files
synced (replays count, as before).

functions.name: sync_vault
functions.doc: Atomize vault notes, map tags/folders to facets. Returns notes synced.

functions.name: freshness
functions.doc:
Honest lexical-vs-semantic readiness (ARCH §3).

Lexical readiness is synchronous (writer commits before ack). Semantic
readiness combines the R01 outbox drain state with the per-revision
projection coverage checklist (INT-1): revisions missing any of
``[segmented, extracted, reconciled, indexed]`` keep ``pending`` honest
even when the outbox queue itself is empty (never vacuous). A revision
counts only while its source pointer serves it; superseded history and
unpointed rows never block readiness. ``index_trusted`` /
``needs_organization`` are computed from these real signals — never
hardcoded.

S2: served from the incrementally maintained coverage state (indexed
lookups + bounded hole page) instead of correlated EXISTS scans.
Existing keys keep exact semantics; the ``coverage_*`` keys are
additive. A high watermark never implies completeness: a derivation
version mismatch forces ``pending`` even with zero holes.

functions.name: _served_relations
functions.doc:
Re-retrieve graph relations scoped to the candidates' revisions.

Read-only dossier-route helper (INT-2): maps each atom-bound candidate
to its served revision, then loads that revision's relation rows
(bounded). Every returned edge carries its ``revision_id``, so the
dossier compiler can prove scope (same visibility/version rules as
candidates); conditions, polarity and endpoint anchors are preserved,
never dropped. Missing graph tables or unresolvable atoms yield no
edges — never an error on the read path.

module_doc:
Query-generated evidence dossiers (R07).

Deterministic, LLM-free compilation of retrieval candidates into an
evidence dossier per ARCHITECTURE §7 / EVALUATION §3:

- Rank against objective TEXT (``goal_state['objective']``), never ``goal_id``.
- Namespace/access/version filters BEFORE text reveal (filter-first ordering;
  storage-layer enforcement stays the caller's job and is stated as such).
- Mandatory constraints + goal context reserved FIRST; mandatory overflow is
  an explicit ``insufficient_budget`` failure, never silent drops.
- Oversized evidence reduced via source-linked anchored excerpts, never
  arbitrary prefixes; an atomic group that cannot fit is an explicit
  coverage failure.
- Conflicting evidence coexists under explicit disagreements; cross-source
  virtual holons are transient (``query_dossier`` kind, derived status with
  lineage — never ground truth).
- Support states (supported/partial/conflicting/insufficient) are assessed
  by a NAMED lexical heuristic (``SUPPORT_METHOD``); lexical overlap does
  not prove sufficiency and is never marketed as NLI.
- Token accounting uses the CONSUMER tokenizer
  (:func:`trace_lite.cordis.models.estimate_tokens`) over content PLUS
  citation wrappers and relation metadata.

Honesty boundary (Cordis adapter): schema conformance is reported
separately from harness loading/use; the Tier-1 lexical action gate stays
labeled ``heuristic``; memory provenance never authorizes execution.

functions.name: objective_relevance
functions.doc:
Hybrid lexical + char-trigram Jaccard against the OBJECTIVE text.

The trigram backoff keeps near-paraphrases retrievable even with weak
word overlap; a zero-lexical paraphrase arriving via the holon route is
still retained by union semantics (route recorded, score honestly low).
``goal_id`` is never consulted.

functions.name: rank_candidates
functions.doc: Stable rank by objective-text relevance (ties keep union order).

functions.name: verify_citation
functions.doc:
Verify an exact byte citation. Returns (valid, method).

Strength ladder (recorded honestly per selection):
``r02_excerpt`` (hash-verified via R02 ``excerpt_span``) >
``source_slice`` (byte slice of the NAMED revision payload — either
resolved server-side from ``revision_id`` via ``conn``, or of a
caller-supplied payload) >
``atom_self`` (self-consistent atom bounds; weakest, labeled as such;
with ``conn`` it is a degraded fallback only — see :func:`compile_dossier`).

functions.name: _atom_binding
functions.doc: Lexical atom id bound to a candidate, if any.

functions.name: resolve_candidate
functions.doc:
Resolve one candidate to (revision_id, span_id, byte range).

Returns ``(enriched, status, reason)`` with ``status`` one of
``RESOLVED``/``DEGRADED``/``INVALID``. Namespace/access/version come from
the serving store (server truth, overriding caller claims); byte bounds
come from the served atom row. Span-anchored candidates adopt their
revision from the span row; whole-atom candidates keep ``span_id`` empty
(their text spans several R02 spans) and verify as ``source_slice``
against the named revision payload.

functions.name: _adopt_scope
functions.doc: Adopt namespace/access/version truth for a span-resolved revision.

functions.name: anchored_excerpt
functions.doc:
Query-anchored window: best objective-term-density slice, byte-exact.

Returns (excerpt, start_byte, end_byte, is_excerpt). Never an arbitrary
prefix: the window centers on the highest term-density anchor; ties go
to the earliest anchor. Byte offsets index the UTF-8 payload and the
slice is decoded on character boundaries.

module_doc: DeepSeek Harness (Cordis/DSH) executive plugin suite.

Qualifier-severance probe fixtures (R08, C8-2).

Each fixture is a single structural paragraph in which an antecedent
condition (negation, unless/only-if, high-contention qualifier, actor or
number qualifier) lives in one sentence and its claim in another. A
predictive cut anywhere *inside* the paragraph separates co-qualifying
sentences into different spans — that is a severed condition. The
structural baseline keeps every fixture in one span (asserted by tests),
so any severance is attributable to the predictive signal alone.

functions.name: count_severance
functions.doc: Number of cuts strictly inside the paragraph (any such cut severs).

module_doc:
Selective-repair comparison fixtures (R08 experimental, EVALUATION §6).

Compares R06-style deterministic dependency-closure invalidation against a
predictive scope estimator (hashbow embedding-residual threshold: skip
repair when the edited assertion's residual is small). Dataset: ordered
source revisions with meaning-changing and meaning-preserving edits plus
the expected affected assertions — the §6 diagnostic in miniature.

The thetas below are a priori reporting points, not tuned values: all
three are reported, none selected on outcomes.

functions.name: base_assertions
functions.doc: One miniature source: a claim, its qualifier, and dependents.

functions.name: edit_cases
functions.doc: Ordered revisions: meaning-changing micro-edits vs preserving edits.

functions.name: deterministic_closure
functions.doc:
R06-style conservative invalidation: edited assertion + every assertion
that transitively depends on it (dependency closure, never skipped).

functions.name: predictive_scope
functions.doc:
Residual-threshold predictor: when the edit's embedding residual is at
most ``theta``, the edit is judged meaning-preserving and no repair is
scheduled (work avoided); otherwise the deterministic closure applies.

functions.name: expected_affected
functions.doc:
Oracle: meaning-changing edits affect target + dependents; preserving
edits affect nothing.

functions.name: compare_all
functions.doc: Run every edit case through both repair policies.

functions.name: summarize
functions.doc: Per-theta tallies + the deterministic baseline under key ``det``.

module_doc:
Apply boundary signals as split-only refinements of structural spans.

``refine_text`` starts from the frozen R02 structural segmentation and
optionally adds cuts *inside* multi-sentence structural spans (never across
them, never merging, never touching code/table/heading spans). Every
refined span is a verbatim sub-slice of exactly one structural span with
exact UTF-8 byte offsets, so the R02 byte contract holds by construction.

Cut rule (frozen a priori, identical for both signals, no qrel tuning):
per structural span, score its inter-sentence candidates, cut at candidates
scoring above the span's own mean + 0.5*std, at most ``MAX_CUTS_PER_SPAN``
cuts, preferred highest-first with spacing enforced by the candidate
generator (``MIN_SIDE_CHARS`` on both sides of every cut).

functions.name: _pick_cuts
functions.doc: Indices of scores above mean + 0.5*std, best-first, capped.

functions.name: refine_text
functions.doc:
Segment ``text`` with the structural baseline plus an optional signal.

``method`` is ``structural`` (R02 baseline, untouched path), ``surprise``
(``+ngram-surprise-trigram``), or ``shift`` (``+hashbow-shift-cos``).

functions.name: refine_cuts
functions.doc:
Character offsets of cuts *added* by the signal (structural → []).

Because refinement is split-only inside structural spans, every interior
boundary of a refined span that lies strictly inside one structural span
is a signal-added cut. Used by the C8-2 qualifier-severance probe.

module_doc:
Embedding-shift delta boundary scorer (R08 experimental).

Scores each candidate cut by the cosine distance between the hashed
bag-of-words vectors of the text windows on either side, using the pinned
R03 hashbow space (``filing.engine.text_vector``: deterministic
sha256(token)-mod-128 counts, L2-normalized; no learned weights, no
downloads). A boundary is shift-like when adjacent windows point in
different directions of that space.

Deterministic: pure function of the text and the frozen window width.

classes.name: EmbeddingShiftSignal
classes.doc: Boundary signal named ``hashbow-shift-cos``.

module_doc:
Character n-gram entropy boundary scorer (R08 experimental).

Fits a character trigram model on the document's own text (no external
corpus, no downloads) and scores each candidate cut by the mean
negative-log-likelihood (surprisal) of the following window. A boundary is
surprising when the text that follows it is unpredictable from the
document's own character statistics.

Deterministic: fixed n, fixed smoothing, dict-iteration-free math.

classes.name: NGramSurpriseSignal
classes.doc: Boundary signal named ``ngram-surprise-trigram``.

module_doc:
R08 experimental predictors (Prediction-Error Atomization + selective repair).

No model downloads, no torch/HF weights (host has no network; HF cache is
empty). Both boundary signals are deterministic CPU heuristics:

- ``surprise``: character trigram surprisal fitted on the document itself.
- ``shift``: local embedding-shift deltas in the pinned R03 hashbow space
  (``filing.engine.text_vector``, 128-d, no learned weights).

Thresholds are per-document adaptive (mean + 0.5*std over the document's
own candidates, max 2 cuts per structural span). Nothing is tuned on any
qrels — DEV runs below are measurements, not selection.

Multi-membership indexing and faceted query over the Hearst forest.

R06 incremental maintenance (ARCH §5–§6): facet centroids are maintained as
O(k*d) running accumulators (unnormalized sum + member count) instead of
O(M*d) full-corpus rescans on every edit. The persisted form is unchanged
(``facets.centroid_blob`` holds the L2-normalized centroid, NULL when
empty); the unnormalized sum lives in RAM and is re-seeded by one exact
scan per facet per process. ``refresh_centroid`` is intentionally left
untouched as the independent exact oracle for parity checks. Membership
rows are still the source of truth: any out-of-band membership change
(direct ``Database.delete_atom``, bulk loads) is detected by
``check_centroid_drift`` / healed by ``reseed_accum``; the writer paths in
``api/app.py`` use ``detach_atom`` / ``assign_facets`` so accums stay exact.

Long-sequence floating-point drift is NOT reconciled here: ``check_drift``

module_doc:
Cross-source holons: overlapping subgraph grouping with reconciliation.

R05 refactor (contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1, ARCHITECTURE §5–§6). The legacy
intra-document-only constraint is replaced by kind-aware validation:

- ``discourse_span``: ordered contiguous spans within one source (legacy
  contract preserved byte-for-byte for this kind).
- ``thematic_cluster``: overlapping cross-source members; topic relation only.
- ``claim_cluster`` (alias ``argument``): cross-source evidence with explicit
  roles (premise/claim/qualification/counterevidence); opposing roles coexist.
- ``query_synthesis`` (aliases ``query_dossier``, ``derived_synthesis``):
  query-assembled virtual holon pinned by dependency rows.

Reconciliation ops are structurally distinct: grouping (membership rows here)
vs linking (typed edge rows in ``holon_link``, see ``reconcile.py``) vs
canonicalizing (versioned mapping rows in ``holon_canonical``). Membership
never implies agreement. Similarity scores can never create identity, support,
contradiction, or causation rows — no such API path exists.

Holons hold memberships, never merged strings (NO text fusion). Containment
is an acyclic depth-bounded DAG; semantic traversals use visited sets and
work budgets. Per-holon accumulators (S_h, W_h, count) update incrementally
in O(k*d) on the pure-add fast path (large holons); small holons re-derive
every field exactly per mutation, and any membership anomaly falls back to
the exact full recompute (the oracle). Descriptor/representatives are exact
on the full path and carried forward on the fold path until the next full
recompute (see ``FULL_REFRESH_LIMIT`` and ``refresh_derived``); digests,
counts, and version history are exact on both paths. Empty holons clear
descriptors.

module_doc:
Selective reconciliation: link vs group vs canonicalize (ARCH §5).

Three structurally distinct ops — never interchangeable:

- ``group``: holon membership rows (``HolonStore`` in ``holon.py``).
- ``link``: a typed relation edge row in ``holon_link``. Closed vocabulary;
  similarity scores can NEVER produce identity, support, contradiction, or
  causation — no API path exists from a score to those relations.
- ``canonicalize``: versioned entity-mapping rows in ``holon_canonical``.
  Aliases are preserved as mapping history; mistaken merges stay reversible
  (``restore_version``) and splittable (``split_canonical``).

Polymorphic endpoints (holon/atom/mention/assertion references) are
code-validated at write time (existence-checked) and re-checked by
``audit_links`` — raw strings are never the only consistency mechanism.

module_doc:
S3 supervised maintenance workers (contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1, steering S3).

Supervised worker lifecycle over the existing R01 outbox / R01 generation
machinery. Workers reuse the exact shared primitives the online
(``ingest_note``) and bulk (``sync_notes``) write paths use —
``source.project.drain_outbox`` (bounded claim -> project -> complete/fail
with the obsolete-revision skip) — so background maintenance can never
diverge from writer-driven correctness. ``source/project.py`` itself is
untouched: the worker is a supervisor around it, not a fork of it.

- Leases: claims carry the R01 lease (30 s floor) inside the shared
  drain. A dead worker's jobs become reclaimable on expiry and a
  restarted worker resumes them with no user replay request.
- Bounded batches: every pass drains at most ``batch_limit`` jobs
  (default: the shared ``DRAIN_LIMIT``; S4 owns tuning).
- Retry/backoff: failed batches back off exponentially via the shared
  ``outbox.retry_delay_s``. The delay is in-memory by design: a restart
  retries immediately, which is always safe because every stage is
  idempotent.
- Backpressure: depth >= high watermark reports pressure; the worker
  keeps draining bounded batches and lexical reads are never blocked.
  Producer-side throttling is S4 scope; S3 delivers the signal plus the
  bound.
- Generation guard: a pass publishes a new ``filing`` generation only
  when it completed real projections. Superseded revisions are
  completed without projecting (the drain's obsolete-worker rule) and
  the stale path never moves the served pointer (see
  ``generations.guarded_activate``).
- Observability: every pass records queue depth, queue lag, and writer
  progress into ``WorkerStats`` and the returned report.

classes.doc: Supervised-worker settings. Defaults reuse shared constants (S4 owns tuning).

classes.name: WorkerStats
classes.doc: Cumulative supervised-lifecycle counters (in-memory, per worker).

classes.name: MaintenanceWorker
classes.doc:
Supervised drain loop over one SQLite file.

Either borrows a caller-owned ``Database`` (single-threaded use,
never closed here) or owns a private handle opened from ``db_path``
(background-thread use: one-instance-per-thread). Work always runs
outside any writer transaction on its own connection.

functions.name: maybe_checkpoint
functions.doc:
Bounded WAL checkpoint + change-log prune at a pass boundary.

G2 cycle 2 contention discipline (worker-owned: only the worker sees
pass boundaries where no txn is open, and ``WalGovernor.checkpoint``
MUST run outside open write txns). Uses the existing governor helper
(``PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)``) when the WAL exceeds the size
threshold; always prunes the atom change log to its retained window
(relocated off the query path). Never raises; every outcome — including
``busy`` (a writer held RESERVED) and ``checkpointed < log`` (readers
pinning snapshots, the checkpoint-starvation signature) — is recorded
in the returned receipt. A call never guarantees truncation: PASSIVE
reclaims only frames no reader pins, and checkpointed frames are
reused by later writes so the file stops growing once checkpoints
keep up. TRUNCATE is deliberately never issued (it would stall the
worker on live readers).

Deterministic structural relation extractor (ARCHITECTURE §4).

Consumes R02 span dicts (``span_id``, ``text``, ``start_byte``, ``end_byte``)
and emits typed :class:`AssertionFrame` / :class:`RelationEdge` values with
exact byte anchors. Rules:

- Supported relationships only: causal keywords (improves, degrades,
  restores, requires, conflicts with), comparison, definitions, reporting /
  reference hooks, and conditions/exceptions (under, unless, only, during,
  when). Anything else yields no frame — never a forced edge.
- Window: one span (≤1200 chars by the R02 cap) plus its recorded heading
  context; long-range links use :func:`find_candidates` (bounded top-k token
  overlap) and bind only on exact unique surfaces — otherwise unresolved.
- Lexical similarity never emits support/contradiction/causation rows.
  Opposing assertions coexist as separate rows; they are never merged.
- Malformed input yields a partial result with warnings. This module never
  raises on data (programming errors from storage layers still raise there).

classes.doc: Extractor output: frames + edges + per-item warnings (never raises).

:class:`EntityMention` rows linked by role; :class:`RelationEdge` rows carry

Source-local evidence graphs (R04): typed assertion frames over R02 spans.

Every record is source-local and evidence-anchored: assertions and relations
resolve to R02 ``evidence_span`` IDs with half-open UTF-8 byte ranges plus the
``extraction_run`` that produced them. Nothing here is a global fact and
nothing is validated — ``epistemic_status`` is ``source_asserted`` unless real
validation lineage exists (it does not in R04), in which case the run records

Parse a markdown note; all spans are UTF-8 byte offsets into `raw`.

Byte-offset mapping (ARCHITECTURE §2):
- ``body_byte_offset``: byte length of the stripped frontmatter block; always
  ``raw.encode()[body_byte_offset:] == body.encode()`` (verified identity,
  never assumed). For CRLF input the offset counts the ``\r`` bytes.
- ``frontmatter_span``: byte range of the stripped block (None when absent).
- ``body_char_offset``: the same boundary in characters (differs from the
  byte offset past any multi-byte content before the body).
- Whitespace trimming by callers (``body.strip()``) has no recorded mapping:
  trimmed text must never be presented as a raw-byte slice.

module_doc:
S5 matched-arms semantic-value trial (contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1).

Compares four arms on a fixed 10-question set (2 per prescribed
category: beyond-top-K, conditional disagreement, quantities, actor
reversal, source updates):

- ``flat``: flat-hybrid baseline (lexical + hashed-BoW dense, RRF top-K).
- ``structural``: baseline + cheap-structure expansion (same section /
  shared wikilink / cluster overlap, bounded, reasoned).
- ``graph``: structural pool + selective evidence-linked groups with
  explicit-syntax roles; costly groups materialized only via
  ``PromotionLedger`` (reused AND useful).
- ``interpret``: bounded query-time interpretation over the structural
  pool — closed explicit-syntax rules only, abstains otherwise.

Utility metrics (steering line 87): unsupported relation rates and
missing counterevidence, NOT relation counts. Exit rule: added
complexity earns its keep iff it improves evidence completeness /
qualifier retention OR reduces repeated work, at equal correctness and
measured cost. R08 stays parked (nothing here predicts or segments).

classes.doc:
Costly groups materialize only when reused AND useful.

Promotion rule (selective): a group is promoted iff at least two
DISTINCT questions used it and at least one use improved evidence
completeness. Single-use or never-useful groups stay computed-once
and are never cached.

Cheap structure for query-native evidence (S5, contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1).

``CHEAP_STRUCTURE_DEF`` is the pre-trial definition required by steering
line 76 / supplement B2. It names the middle ground between the dead
open-domain 14-verb regex triples (the floor to beat, NOT the structure
arm) and a local SLM on every sentence (explicitly NOT proposed here —
no false dichotomy):

- structural markdown hierarchy: sections, lists, callouts, tables,
  code fences, wikilinks — all byte-anchored;
- entity co-occurrence clusters: capitalized noun phrases, wikilink
  targets and tags co-occurring inside one structural block, with
  byte-anchored mention spans.

No verb patterns, no triples, no model calls. Everything in this module
is deterministic syntax over the raw note bytes.

module_doc:
R03 encoder wrapper: pinned sparse-projection encoder (packet fallback).

DEGRADED — no learned weights. Host has no network (B1 probe:
``Network is unreachable``), ``usearch``/``onnxruntime`` are not installed and
the HuggingFace cache is empty, so no transformer weights can be fetched.
This module therefore pins the exact sparse space the frozen BEIR baselines
were measured in and labels it honestly instead of claiming learned quality.

Pinned configuration (part of the encoder identity / config hash):
  tokenizer:      ``filing`` word regex ``[a-z0-9_]+`` (casefolded);
                  all-digit tokens excluded from vectors (serial/year guard)
  weights:        none — deterministic sha256(token) mod 128 hashed counts
  pooling:        count-sum over vector tokens
  normalization:  L2 unit norm, then corpus IDF ``log((N+1)/(df+1))+1``
                  reweight + L2 renormalize (same as FlatHybrid.warm)
  dim:            128

A future learned encoder plugs in beside this one by implementing the same
``encode``/``config_hash`` surface and flipping ``degraded`` to False; the
index manifest records which encoder built it so generations never mix.

classes.doc: Pinned encoder identity. ``config_hash`` binds index generations.

classes.doc: Exact wrapper around the pinned sparse projection (+ IDF weighting).

Warmed dense matrix (numpy) + FTS5 sparse side, fused with RRF.

Matrix rows are IDF-weighted hashed-BoW vectors: without IDF, a 300-token

prunes. The worker/drain calls this after a pass (same bound, same
gap-fallback contract for lagging readers).

module_doc:
R03 embedded ANN: numpy IVF index + crash-recoverable publication.

Fallback substrate (no network — see ``encoder.py``): IVF over the pinned
``hashbow-128-idf`` space. Same vectors, same filters, same budgets as the
exact path; recall is measured against brute force, never against qrels.

Publication protocol (ARCH §8: immutable segments + manifests):
  1. write segment files, flush + fsync
  2. write ``manifest-<gen>.json`` via tmp + os.replace, fsync dir
  3. publish ``CURRENT`` pointer via tmp + os.replace, fsync dir
  4. record + activate the ``projection_generation`` row (kind
     ``vector_index``) — readers pin the generation CURRENT names
Deletes never rewrite segments: they append to an immutable-per-write
``tombstones-<gen>.json`` delta loaded alongside the manifest. Files no
manifest references are orphans: reported on open, collectable, never fatal.

classes.doc: In-memory IVF over one encoder space + file publication helpers.

functions.doc:

functions.doc: Bounded Lloyd k-means with kmeans++ init. Deterministic for fixed seed.

module_doc:
INT-3 learned encoder: pinned BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 behind the INT-2 seam.

Spike (contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1): prove or disprove learned retrieval on
the SERVED path. Either outcome is acceptable if measured.

Pinned configuration (part of the encoder identity / config hash):
  weights:        HF ``BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`` @ revision
                  ``5c38ec7c405ec4b44b94cc5a9bb96e735b38267a``
  tokenizer:      bert-base-uncased WordPiece (model-pinned ``vocab.txt``),
                  lowercase; 512-token model limit
  prompts:        none on either side (symmetric passage encoding for docs
                  and queries; no ``Represent this sentence`` prefix)
  pooling:        CLS token (model-pinned ``1_Pooling`` config:
                  ``pooling_mode_cls_token=true``)
  normalization:  L2 unit norm (``normalize_embeddings=True``)
  dim:            384

Long-span policy (never silent truncation): texts longer than 510 content
tokens are split into overlapping WordPiece windows (510 tokens, stride 458,
i.e. 52-token overlap, decoded back to text), each window is encoded, and
the window vectors are mean-pooled + L2-renormalized. The build records how
many texts were chunked (``chunked_texts``/``chunk_windows``); queries take
the same path, so docs and queries share one code path.

Interface: implements the INT-2 encoder seam (``fit_idf`` /
``encode_weighted`` / ``config_hash`` / ``spec`` / ``dim`` / ``degraded``)
plus ``encode_many`` for bounded-batch corpus builds. ``fit_idf``/``set_idf``
are seam-compatible no-ops (a learned space has no IDF) that record the
corpus size. ``degraded`` is False (real weights).

The module imports light: ``torch``/``sentence_transformers`` load lazily
inside :meth:`LearnedBgeEncoder.load` so the library and test suite never
pay the import cost unless weights are actually used. When weights are
unavailable the factory raises a named ``WeightsMissingError`` and callers
keep the hashbow fallback (see ``served_default``).

Raised when learned weights cannot be loaded (no snapshot, no network).

Retrieval stems but coverage scoring did not: a doc FTS-matched via shared

gate thresholds saw weaker evidence than the index actually found.

functions.name: lexical_search
functions.doc:
FTS5-backed keyword search with LIKE fallback. Returns atom dicts + score.

AND-first: conjunctive matches rank cheapest (indexed intersection); OR only
supplements when AND yields fewer than `limit` rows. Same recall, far less sorting.
Unranked by default: BM25 ORDER BY scores every match (25k+ rows for common
terms); match-fraction order then provides the ranking. Pass ranked=True
for the quality profile: BM25 order wins outright on prose claims.
`pool` overrides the default limit*3 candidate depth per clause.

functions.name: has_lexical_support
functions.doc:
True when query terms (or stems) appear in candidate anchor text.

Corroboration signal for the abstention gate: dense-only matches with zero
lexical support are hash-collision noise in this substrate, not evidence.
Checking the candidate anchor text specifically prevents database-wide leakage
where an unrelated note's terms incorrectly corroborate a false anchor.

Signatures supported:
  has_lexical_support(conn, query, anchor_text=...)
  has_lexical_support(query, anchor_text)
  has_lexical_support(conn, query)  # legacy db-wide fallback
  has_lexical_support(query="...", anchor_text="...")
  has_lexical_support(conn=..., query="...", anchor_text="...")

module_doc:
R03 projection workers: bounded-batch encoding outside the writer lock.

Model/embedding work must never hold the database writer lock (ARCH §8): the
worker reads pinned atom rows on its own connection, encodes in bounded
batches, and publishes through the index adapter's save→manifest→CURRENT→
generation-row protocol. Late output for a superseded watermark never
overwrites the active generation (watermark check before publish).

functions.name: iter_atom_batches
functions.doc: Read-only, bounded batches in rowid order (no writer lock held).

functions.name: encode_batches
functions.doc: Yield (ids, IDF-weighted normalized matrix) per bounded batch.

functions.name: build_and_publish
functions.doc:
Two-pass build (IDF fit, then encode) + crash-safe publish.

``check_watermark``: when set, abort without publishing if the CURRENT
manifest's watermark already supersedes this build (late-worker guard).
Returns the publish receipt plus encoder identity.

module_doc:
S4 persistent vector serving: cached embeddings + published base + bounded delta.

Steady-state contract (steering S4 row + line 85 methodology):

- Embedding outputs are cached keyed by (content sha256, encoder config
  hash); distinct source occurrences keep per-atom entries that may share
  one cached vector. A one-source edit encodes only the changed content
  (steady state: 1 encode, never a corpus re-encode).
- Vector *generation* (delta overlay + background compaction) is separate
  from the *published base*: readers open the CURRENT generation and keep
  serving it while a new generation is staged; the CURRENT flip is the
  single atomic publication step (``os.replace``), reusing the R03
  save -> manifest -> CURRENT -> generation-row protocol.
- The served view is ``published base + bounded delta/tombstones``. Delta
  size is bounded (``delta_bound``); breaching it requires compaction
  (merge into a new published generation). Tuning the bound is out of
  scope (S4 contract); the default is a plain constant.
- Hashbow IDF is frozen per served epoch (steering line 65): the epoch
  ``(config_hash, idf, doc_count)`` is recorded in the per-generation
  sidecar and inherited by the delta overlay. Compaction merges under the
  SAME epoch (never a silent IDF change); a new IDF epoch needs one
  explicit background rebuild (the transitional-repair path), never a
  query-triggered one.
- First query never builds: :meth:`ServedVectors.open` and
  :func:`ensure_served_persistent` only open what is published. With no
  published base they report detached/fallback instead of encoding.
- Crash coherence at every publication boundary comes from atomic file
  replacement plus generation-scoped sidecars (``s4-delta-<gen>.json``):
  a torn write can only leave a ``*.tmp`` file the opener ignores, and a
  CURRENT flip without its sidecar heals deterministically because the
  flipped generation already contains the merged content (see
  :meth:`ServedVectors.recover`).

File layout inside ``index_dir`` (shares the R03 directory; every S4 file
uses an ``s4-`` prefix so R03 orphan scans never match it):

- R03 files, untouched: ``segments/seg-<gen>.*.npy``,
  ``manifest-<gen>.json``, ``tombstones-<gen>.json``, ``CURRENT``.
- ``s4-delta-<gen>.json``: per-generation sidecar carrying the frozen IDF
  epoch plus the bounded overlay (upserts keyed by atom id, tombstones).
  Always written, even when the overlay is empty.
- ``s4-cache.json`` (optional): persisted embedding cache. Losing it is
  safe (a miss re-encodes); mixing encoder configs is refused on load.

classes.name: EmbeddingCache
classes.doc:
Content-keyed cache of RAW (unweighted) encoder vectors.

The cache stores the IDF-free base form (:meth:`HashBowEncoder.encode`);
weighting with the generation's frozen IDF happens in
:class:`ServedVectors`, so one cached entry serves every IDF epoch.
``encodes`` counts real encoder calls (cache misses); ``hits`` counts
deduped re-encodes avoided. Both are the S4 update-cost evidence.

classes.name: ServedVectors
classes.doc:
S4 serving layer over one R03 index directory.

``open()`` loads the CURRENT published base plus its sidecar and never
encodes or writes. Mutation (``ingest_atom``/``delete_atom``) touches
only the bounded in-memory overlay and its sidecar file. ``publish()``
compacts base + overlay into a new published generation through the
crash-safe R03 protocol. All corpus text encoding flows through the
shared :class:`EmbeddingCache`, which is also the update-cost meter.

functions.name: ensure_served_persistent
functions.doc:
Pin the S4 served view on a router. Never builds, never encodes corpus.

Drop-in replacement for the query-triggered full-corpus build: when a
published base (or overlay) is servable the merged in-memory view is
attached to the router's existing ANN branch (all INT-2 filtering
semantics unchanged); otherwise the branch detaches with an honest note
and the named lexical fallbacks serve. Corpus encode count is provably
unchanged (only the per-query vector encodes, as with every branch).

module_doc: Sub-50ms 3-tier dual-dispatch retrieval router.

A ``BoundarySignal`` scores candidate cut points (character offsets) inside
one text. Experimental refiners in ``trace_lite.experimental`` map chosen
cuts to byte-exact spans. This module adds no behavior to
``segmentation.py`` / ``views.py`` (both untouched); it only declares the
protocol, a registry, and shared byte-exact splitting helpers.

classes.doc: Scores candidate cut offsets; higher means more boundary-like.

functions.doc: Register a signal implementation under its ``name``.

functions.name: get
functions.doc: Fetch a registered signal by name (``KeyError`` when unknown).

functions.name: names
functions.doc: Registered signal names, sorted.

functions.doc:
Inter-sentence char offsets eligible as cut points.

Only boundaries with at least ``min_side`` characters on each side are
returned, in increasing order. Deterministic.

functions.name: char_span_to_bytes
functions.doc: Map a char slice to exact UTF-8 half-open byte offsets (no estimation).

module_doc:
S2 materialized projection coverage (contract TL-QN-2026-09-12.1).

Query-path problem: ``freshness``/``pending_coverage`` ran correlated
``EXISTS`` scans over ``source_revision`` x segmentation/extraction/
grouping/job rows on EVERY query (~15 s tax at 10 k pending). S2 makes
every query-path read an indexed lookup over state maintained
incrementally on the write/drain paths.

Design (STEERING S2 row):

- ``revision_coverage``: one row per revision, per-stage checklist flags
  (seg/ext/rec/idx) + ``has_pending_job`` + ``in_scope`` + derived
  ``pending``/``missing``/``reason``. Maintained by SQLite triggers on
  the write path (revision insert, scope-pointer moves, stage-output
  inserts, job insert/update, grouping changes): each trigger touches
  only the affected revision row via indexed lookups — O(1) per write,
  never a recomputation.
- ``coverage_hole``: explicit hole set — every pending revision below
  the watermark with its reason (missing stages + job error). Synced by
  triggers on ``revision_coverage`` itself, so it can never disagree
  with the checklist. Hole enumeration on the read path is bounded
  (cap + truncated flag).
- ``coverage_meta``: ``projection_version`` + ``max_observed_at``
  watermark (single-row PK lookups on the read path).
- A high watermark NEVER implies completeness: ``freshness`` reports
  pending whenever the hole set is non-empty OR the materialized
  projection version differs from code (version changes surface as
  pending even with zero holes).
- ``recompute_pending_coverage`` is the exact pre-S2 scan, kept as the
  test oracle: materialized state must equal recomputation after every
  transition sequence (see tests/test_bounded_reads.py).
- Counts use partial indexes (``pending = 1``; live job states), so
  they are O(pending), drift-free, and need no counter triggers.

Write-path repair (drain start): ``ensure_coverage_schema`` is
idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS everywhere) and heals only pending rows plus
any rows missing since the last drain — bounded by pending/new, never
a full recompute. Full recompute happens only in migration/backfill
and on projection-version change (rare, write path).

functions.doc:
Recompute derived columns from flags for the touched rows only.

Two ordered statements (derived, then reason) so no statement reads
a column assigned earlier in the same statement.

functions.name: _ensure_row_sql
functions.doc: Ensure a coverage row exists for a revision known only by id.

functions.name: _job_flags_sql
functions.doc: Refresh idx/has_pending_job/job_error for one revision's jobs.

functions.name: _rec_from_grouping_sql
functions.doc: Recompute rec from live grouping for the touched rows only.

functions.name: recompute_flags_for_revision
functions.doc:
Exact per-revision flags from base rows (test oracle, write path only).

Mirrors the pre-S2 ``coverage_for_revision``/``pending_coverage``
stage semantics plus the in-scope bit. Never called on the query path.

functions.name: recompute_pending_coverage
functions.doc: Byte-for-byte pre-S2 ``pending_coverage`` scan (oracle only).

functions.name: ensure_coverage_schema
functions.doc:
Idempotent DDL + bounded heal (write/drain path only, never queries).

Creates tables, partial indexes, and triggers (holon triggers only
once grouping tables exist), defaults the meta rows, then heals:
backfills rows for revisions missing since the last call (gated by
counts, so the common case is two O(1) counts) and re-derives flags
for pending rows only (bounded by pending, via indexed point reads).

functions.name: _heal_coverage
functions.doc: Bounded repair: missing rows + pending-row re-derivation.

functions.name: _rederive_one
functions.doc: Re-derive one row from the oracle; True when the row changed.

functions.name: _reason_for
functions.doc: Python mirror of the trigger reason text (must stay identical).

functions.name: backfill_from_recompute
functions.doc:
Full re-derivation from base rows (migration/backfill path only).

Rebuilds every coverage row from the oracle, rebuilds the hole set,
and stamps the watermark + version. O(revisions); never on queries.

functions.name: verify_against_oracle
functions.doc:
Equivalence check: materialized state vs exact recomputation.

Returns ``{"mismatches": [...], "checked": N}``. Empty mismatches
means the incremental triggers agree with the full scan exactly.
Compares stage flags, scope, pending bit, missing set, and the hole
set against the oracle pending list. Write/test path only.

functions.name: maybe_heal_version
functions.doc:
Drain-start version gate: stale derivation re-derives, then heals.

When the materialized version differs from code, every freshness
read already reports pending (see ``freshness_snapshot``); the drain
repairs by full backfill so the next read is exact again. Returns
``{"healed": bool}``.

functions.name: pending_from_state
functions.doc: Bounded pending page + exact total (partial-index count).

functions.name: hole_page
functions.doc: Bounded hole enumeration + total + truncated flag.

functions.name: freshness_snapshot
functions.doc:
All materialized inputs a freshness read needs (indexed lookups).

No base-table scans: two partial-index counts, one meta PK lookup
each for version + watermark, one bounded hole page.

functions.name: explain_plan
functions.doc: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN detail strings for one read statement.

module_doc:
INT-1 projection pipeline: bounded synchronous drain over R01/R02/R04/R05.

Wires the verified library components into one per-write pipeline:

``segment`` (R02 ``views``) -> ``extract`` (R04 extractor + graph store)
-> ``reconcile`` (R05 ``HolonStore`` corpus grouping) -> ``index``
(job drained; the served lexical publication is the ``filing`` generation
bump owned by the caller in ``api/app.py``).

Single-node, bounded, synchronous: every served write drains the outbox
under the writer lock before ack, so readers never observe silent lag.
Each revision carries a coverage checklist
``[segmented, extracted, reconciled, indexed]`` computed live from existing
rows (no migration): ``freshness`` reports revisions with incomplete
coverage even when the outbox queue is empty (never vacuous).

Idempotency: every stage checks for existing output before writing, so a
replay (same key + payload, ``created=False``) or a resume drain never
duplicates spans, runs, or holon memberships.

Reconciliation policy (minimal, honest): the pipeline groups each
revision's lexical atom into one pipeline-maintained ``thematic_cluster``
corpus holon (cross-source grouping; membership never implies agreement,
and no similarity score ever mints a typed link — R05). Typed links and
canonical entities stay manual. Corpus creation needs >= 2 atoms, so a
first lone revision reports ``reconciled=False`` with an explicit reason
until a second atom arrives (backfilled on the next drain). The corpus
holon is pipeline-maintained (state refreshed synchronously by
``add_members``), so invalidation callers exclude it: only downstream
syntheses go stale on premise edits.

Obsolete-worker rule (ARCH section 3 step 5): a refresh job whose revision
is no longer current is completed WITHOUT projecting (late output never
overwrites current projections); retract jobs carry no projections (the
caller invalidates synchronously from its pre-write snapshot).

classes.name: ProjectionError
classes.doc: A revision's projection failed; source retained, pending explicit.

functions.name: reset_contention_state
functions.doc: Reset drain-throttle clocks (tests/probes only; production never calls).

functions.name: _is_busy_error
functions.doc: True for transient SQLite lock contention (SQLITE_BUSY / locked).

functions.name: _retry_on_busy
functions.doc:
Run idempotent ``fn`` with bounded busy retry (rollback before retry).

Non-busy errors propagate immediately. When attempts exhaust, the last
busy error propagates (callers convert to held/deferred, never fatal).

functions.name: _has_holon_tables
functions.doc:
Whether grouping tables exist on this file yet.

``holons``/``holon_members`` come from the filing ``HOLON_SCHEMA``
(ensured lazily by ``HolonStore``), not the static ``schema.sql`` — so a
file that never ran a grouping has no such tables. Coverage then reports
``reconciled=False`` honestly instead of raising; the write path
ensures the DDL via ``HolonStore`` before grouping.

functions.name: coverage_for_revision
functions.doc: Live coverage checklist for one revision from existing rows.

functions.name: revisions_in_scope
functions.doc:
Currently served revisions: the ones source pointers select.

Only pointed-to revisions gate readiness (current-mode results are
version-filtered). Superseded history and unpointed ad-hoc rows (e.g. a
manually injected outbox probe with no source pointer) never block it.

functions.name: pending_coverage
functions.doc:
In-scope revisions missing >= 1 coverage stage (bounded, one query).

S2: served from the incrementally maintained ``revision_coverage``
state (partial-index page, never a pending-table scan). Contract
unchanged: same order, same dict shape, same default cap. Files
whose coverage state was never ensured (pre-S2 library use) fall
back to the exact recomputation oracle.

functions.name: find_corpus_holon
functions.doc: Id of the pipeline-maintained corpus holon (None when absent).

functions.name: _backfill_candidates
functions.doc: Other served atoms still ungrouped (oldest first, bounded).

functions.name: ensure_grouped
functions.doc:
Group atoms into the corpus holon. Returns grouped/deferred + reason.

Idempotent: already-grouped atoms are skipped, never duplicated (the
store raises on duplicate membership, so the check-before-add is the
replay guard). A lone first atom defers honestly: corpus creation
needs >= 2 atoms.

functions.name: _project_segment_extract
functions.doc:
Run the segment -> extract stages for one revision (idempotent).

Shared by :func:`project_revision` and the batched
:func:`drain_outbox` path so both observe identical stage semantics.
Returns the complete segmentation ``view_id`` on success, else None
(the failure is already recorded + noted on ``report``).

functions.name: _apply_grouping_outcome
functions.doc:
Fold one batched ``ensure_grouped`` outcome into a revision report.

Same per-revision semantics as the reconcile tail of
:func:`project_revision`: grouped/already-grouped atoms reconcile, a
deferred atom records a ``projection.failed`` event for the
``reconciled`` stage and stays pending for the next pass.

functions.name: project_revision
functions.doc:
Run segment -> extract -> reconcile for one revision (idempotent).

Each stage reuses existing output when present. Returns a stage report;
a failed stage records a ``projection.failed`` event and stops the
pipeline with the source retained (partial coverage stays explicit via
:func:`coverage_for_revision`). Never raises on data errors.

functions.name: _maybe_heal_coverage
functions.doc:
Throttled coverage-schema ensure (drain path only, never queries).

The DDL ensure is idempotent and the triggers maintain the state
incrementally; the expensive part (walking every pending row) only
repairs drift, so it runs at most every ``HEAL_MIN_INTERVAL_S`` per
file — plus always when the tables are absent, on the first call per
file, and on the grouping-table creation transition (when the holon
triggers can first exist). A persistently busy heal is SKIPPED
(triggers keep the state fresh; the next pass retries) — never fatal
to the drain.

functions.name: _group_defer_reason
functions.doc:
Why this pass must skip grouping ("" = group now).

A cascaded atom delete (R01 edit/retract) invalidates the corpus fold
gate, flipping the next grouping into a full O(corpus) recompute inside
ONE write txn (measured 2.95 s at 4 k members). While drift is detected
on a large corpus, grouping runs at most every ``GROUP_MIN_PASSES``
passes so one full recompute absorbs every batched cascade instead of
one per pass. The check is two indexed point reads (no member scan).
Small corpuses and the corpus-creation path never defer.

functions.name: _is_current
functions.doc: Obsolete-worker check: is this revision still the served one?

functions.name: drain_outbox
functions.doc:
Claim -> project -> complete/failed over pending jobs (bounded).

- refresh job, revision still current: run segment -> extract, then
  group the whole pass's atoms with ONE :func:`ensure_grouped` call
  (R1 batching: the holon fold re-scans all member texts per call, so
  per-job grouping is O(N) per job and O(N^2) per drain; one call per
  pass amortizes it by the batch size). Complete on full coverage,
  fail (retryable, error recorded) otherwise.
- refresh job, revision superseded: complete without projecting (late
  output never overwrites current projections).
- retract job: complete without projecting (the write path invalidates
  synchronously from its pre-write snapshot).
- poison guard: a job seen twice in one call is left pending.
- G1 fairness: a failing job HOLDS its claim while the pass continues
  to later jobs (a lone-atom deferral must never head-of-line block a
  retract behind it); held claims release to pending at pass end.
- contention discipline (G2 cycle 2): the pass's atoms group in
  ``GROUP_COMMIT_CHUNK``-atom commits with yields between (no single
  write txn spans a full 64-job projection); the claim loop paces
  itself so concurrent writers find acquisition gaps; the coverage
  heal is throttled (triggers maintain the state); grouping defers
  under large-corpus drift so one full recompute absorbs batched
  cascades instead of one per pass. Deferred jobs release to pending
  (reported under ``deferred``, never ``failed``) and converge on a
  later pass. Obsolete-skip, idempotency, and return shape preserved
  (new keys are additive).

module_doc:
Structural source segmentation (R02): byte-faithful evidence spans.

Structural baseline only (paragraphs, bullets, headings, atomic code fences and
markdown tables, conversation turns / log events where applicable). No
ML/perplexity boundary detection (R08 non-goal).

Byte contract (ARCHITECTURE §2): every span is a UTF-8 half-open byte range
``[start_byte, end_byte)`` into the retained raw payload, and ``span.text ==
raw_bytes[start_byte:end_byte].decode("utf-8")`` always holds. Span text is the
verbatim raw slice — no trimming that moves a boundary without moving the
offset, no normalization. A normalized-text offset must never claim raw-byte
identity, so this module performs no normalization at all.

Whitespace rule: only whole blank boundary lines are dropped; every kept line is
stored verbatim (including CRLF and indentation). The byte range always covers
exactly the returned text.

Length cap: paragraph/bullet/turn spans are capped at ``MAX_SPAN_CHARS`` (1200),
split on sentence boundaries. Code fences and markdown tables are atomic and
stay undivided even over the cap (structural integrity wins; C2-3).

Repeated identical text: spans are distinguished by ordinal occurrence, so each
occurrence gets a separate span ID downstream (ARCHITECTURE §2).

classes.doc: One structural span with verified raw-byte coordinates.

functions.doc: Split text into lines (kept endings) with each line's start byte offset.

Segment raw markdown-ish text into byte-faithful structural spans.

``body_byte_base`` shifts every span's byte range (used when segmenting a

address the retained raw payload, with the mapping recorded on the view).

module_doc:
Source service: atomic replacement with retained revisions (R01).

One writer transaction per replacement: insert revision + update the
current-source pointer + lexical delta (``atom``/``fts_atoms`` rows) + compact
event + outbox job. Expensive projection work never runs here; workers consume
the outbox outside the writer transaction.

Concurrency: pass ``expected_revision`` for conflicting edits; a stale value is
rejected with :class:`ObsoleteRevisionError` (EVALUATION gate 5). Idempotency:
``(key, payload_hash) -> revision_id``; same key + different payload raises
:class:`IdempotencyConflict` naming the key (gate 2). Crash seam: the private
``_pre_commit_fault`` closed-over hook runs inside the writer transaction just
before commit (gate 3 test seam; not a global).

Same source + same payload replays to the prior revision (``publish``
returns ``created=False`` with no new outbox job); any payload change
mints a fresh key and therefore a new revision. The same-key/different-
payload conflict path stays available to explicit-key library callers.

module_doc:
Versioned segmentation views over retained source revisions (R02).

An ``evidence_span`` row is immutable once written: ``span_id`` derives from
``(revision_id, run_id, ordinal, start_byte, end_byte)`` so re-segmentation
with a new run/config id mints new span IDs and never rewrites prior rows. A
``segmentation_view`` row groups one run's spans; alternatives coexist and prior
references keep resolving.

Failure rule (packet recovery): a segmentation failure produces a retained
revision with a ``status='partial'`` view row carrying zero spans — never
fabricated offsets.

functions.doc: Deterministic, per-view span identity (repeats get separate ordinals).

Segment a retained revision and persist spans + a new view row.

Reads the revision's retained text from ``source_revision`` (the canonical
payload). ``body_byte_base`` + ``signal`` record the verified byte mapping
when segmenting a transformed slice (e.g. a frontmatter-stripped body):
body-relative offsets are shifted so stored spans address raw payload bytes.
Returns ``{"view_id", "run_id", "revision_id", "span_ids", "status", ...}``.
