Single-node SQLite storage engine: canonical atoms, event ledger, FTS5 index.

classes.name: Database
classes.doc: Owns one SQLite file in WAL mode. Not thread-safe; one instance per thread.

functions.name: ensure_atom_delta_log
functions.doc:
Idempotent change-log DDL (additive; safe on every open).

Rows changed before the first ensure are covered by the reader's next
full-warm baseline, which watermarks at the then-current max ``seq``.

module_doc:
Versioned projection generations (R01 migration 001).

R01 only freezes the record shape (ARCH §2: kind, config hash, watermark,
manifest, active status) and the activation primitive used when a worker
publishes output. Real generation kinds are owned by R02+; the ``refresh``
kind used here marks lexical-readiness acknowledgment.

functions.name: activate_generation
functions.doc:
Activate a generation as the sole active row of its kind.

The swap is one atomic single-statement ``UPDATE`` (CASE over the kind),
so concurrent activations can never leave zero or two active rows.

When ``expected_active_id`` is given, the UPDATE carries a
compare-and-swap guard: the swap happens only if that generation is
still the kind's active one, decided by the statement's rowcount.
A mismatch returns False with the DB unchanged -- a lost race is a
defined outcome, never an exception. Unknown ``generation_id`` still
raises KeyError (a programming error, not a lost race).

``commit=False`` joins the caller's transaction (no BEGIN/COMMIT/
rollback issued); the exactly-one-winner race guarantee across
connections then needs the caller to hold the write lock
(BEGIN IMMEDIATE). With ``commit=True`` this takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE
itself when it owns the txn boundary; a mismatch then rolls back to
release the lock and never commits.

functions.name: guarded_activate
functions.doc:
Activate a generation only when the worker output is still current.

S3 generation guard: a worker that computed output from a superseded
revision must NEVER move the served pointer. Callers compute
``allow`` from a currency check (e.g. the revision is still the
source's current revision at publish time) and call this to publish.
When ``allow`` is False the active generation is left untouched and
the call reports ``{"activated": False, ...}`` — stale output is
skipped, never served.

The ``allow=True`` path publishes through the atomic CAS activation:
pass ``expected_active_id`` (the generation the caller saw as active)
to make the currency check itself atomic — a concurrent publisher
winning first turns this call into ``{"activated": False, ...}``
with the DB unchanged instead of silently overriding the winner.

module_doc:
Active WAL Checkpoint Governor.

Issues ``PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)`` every ``threshold`` committed
documents. Must run strictly outside open write transactions (post-commit):
calling it mid-transaction raises ``database table is locked`` (CRIT-04).

classes.name: WalGovernor
classes.doc: Counts committed documents; checkpoints post-commit at each threshold.

module_doc:
Legacy migration tool: R01 migration 001 (ARCH §9).

Snapshots the live database with ``VACUUM INTO`` (consistent backup) BEFORE any
schema write, applies the migration-001 DDL, then backfills exactly one legacy
``source_revision`` per ``doc_id`` in a single transaction:

- single-atom doc: revision text is that atom's text, byte-exact; the revision
  links the atom row (``atom_id``) so scoped lexical search keeps working.
- multi-atom doc: revision text is the atoms' texts joined by ``"\n"`` in atom-id
  order; ``legacy_atom_map`` records per-atom ``(start_char, end_char)`` offsets
  so every legacy atom stays byte-exact recoverable.

Migrated revisions are labeled ``coordinate_space = 'legacy_atom_text'``: the
original raw offsets cannot be reconstructed from zero-based body offsets
(ARCH §2). The ``atom`` table and every existing ``Database`` method keep working
(compat shim, not rewrite). Reruns are safe: when ``schema_version >= 1`` and
every atom is mapped, the backfill is skipped and parity is re-verified.
Parity < 100% raises :class:`MigrationParityError` without committing.

classes.name: MigrationParityError
classes.doc: Raised when migrated text is not 100% faithful to the legacy atoms.

functions.name: snapshot_backup
functions.doc: Write a consistent snapshot of the live DB via ``VACUUM INTO``.

functions.name: migrate_legacy
functions.doc: Migrate a legacy store to migration 001. Returns the parity report dict.

functions.name: migrate_spans_002
functions.doc:
Apply R02 migration 002: add ``evidence_span`` + ``segmentation_view``.

Purely additive: no existing table is altered or dropped, so rollback is
restoring the ``.bak-002`` snapshot (or simply staying on the pre-002 file).
The ``schema_version = 2`` row is written ONLY here — never by the static
DDL — so migration-001 callers keep observing ``MAX(schema_version) == 1``
until they opt into 002. Reruns are safe (idempotent ``IF NOT EXISTS`` DDL
plus ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` of the version row).

functions.name: migrate_graph_003
functions.doc:
Apply R04 migration 003: add local-graph tables (ARCH §2 records).

Purely additive: no existing table is altered or dropped, so rollback is
restoring the ``.bak-003`` snapshot (or simply staying on the pre-003
file). The ``schema_version = 3`` row is written ONLY here — never by the
static DDL — so migration-001/002 callers keep observing their
``MAX(schema_version)`` values until they opt into 003. Reruns are safe
(idempotent ``IF NOT EXISTS`` DDL plus ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` of the
version row). This contract is frozen for R05: later packets may add
tables but must not alter these six.

functions.name: migrate_holon_004
functions.doc:
Apply R05 migration 004: cross-source holon + reconciliation tables.

Purely additive: no existing table is altered (``holon_members`` gains
columns only via ``ADD COLUMN`` with defaults) or dropped, so rollback is
restoring the ``.bak-004`` snapshot (or simply staying on the pre-004
file). Legacy holon IDs and memberships are preserved byte-for-byte;
every legacy holon gains a ``holon_state`` row (kind ``discourse_span``).
The ``schema_version = 4`` row is written ONLY here — never by the static
DDL — so migration-001/002/003 callers keep observing their
``MAX(schema_version)`` values until they opt into 004. Reruns are safe.
This contract is frozen for R06/R07: later packets may add tables but
must not alter these five.

functions.name: migrate_coverage_005
functions.doc:
Apply S2 migration 005: materialized coverage state (ARCH §2 records).

Purely additive: three new tables, partial/support indexes, and
triggers — no existing table is altered or dropped, so rollback is
restoring the ``.bak-005`` snapshot (or staying on the pre-005 file).
The ``schema_version = 5`` row is written ONLY here, so earlier
callers keep observing their ``MAX(schema_version)`` values until
they opt into 005. Reruns are safe (idempotent ``IF NOT EXISTS``
DDL plus ``INSERT OR IGNORE`` of the version row; an already-current
file is re-verified, not rewritten).

Equivalence protocol (S2 oracle rule): the backfill is first applied
on a scratch ``VACUUM INTO`` copy and checked against the exact
recomputation; only then is the live file backfilled and re-checked.
Any disagreement raises :class:`MigrationParityError` without
writing the version row.

functions.name: _verify_coverage_live
functions.doc: Re-verify an already-migrated file against the oracle (no rewrite).

functions.name: _check_006_equivalence
functions.doc:
Oracle diff for 006 (A1 §5.3): empty-table migration must disturb nothing.

(i) atom count + full-table hash identical; (ii) fixed FTS probe set
returns identical rowids; (iii) tombstone table exists post-DDL — empty
when absent pre-DDL, byte-identical when the file already carried rows
(Database open auto-applies schema.sql, so live files may); (iv) DDL
alone moves no version row.

functions.name: migrate_tombstones_006
functions.doc:
Apply A1 migration 006: add ``atom_tombstone`` + ``idx_tombstone_gen``.

Purely additive: no existing table is altered or dropped, so rollback is
restoring the ``.bak-006`` snapshot (or staying on the pre-006 file).
The ``schema_version = 6`` row is written ONLY here — never by the static
DDL — so migration-001..005 callers keep observing their
``MAX(schema_version)`` values until they opt into 006. Reruns are safe
(an already-current file is re-verified, not rewritten).

Equivalence protocol (005 pattern): the DDL is first applied on a
scratch ``VACUUM INTO`` copy and checked against the oracle; only then is
the live file migrated and re-checked. Any disagreement raises
:class:`MigrationParityError` without writing the version row.

Known limitation (A1 §5.5, documented not fixed): atoms physically
deleted BEFORE 006 leave no tombstone; their ids resolve as unknown,
never false-retired.

functions.name: _verify_tombstones_live
functions.doc: Re-verify an already-migrated file (no rewrite).

module_doc:
MAP-09 mint counter primitives (N06a DES/DUR/FAIL, N06b RST/U/C/A, D4).

Greenfield relative to ``store/generations.py`` (N06a section 9): this module
owns the fenced ``mint_epoch`` row + per-``(mint_epoch, generation_id)``
counter rows. It never imports or modifies ``generations.py``.

Caller-transaction contract: every primitive takes an open
``sqlite3.Connection`` and NEVER commits (or rolls back) internally. The
caller couples the mint to its publication transaction (DES-6/DES-12/DUR-1)
and commits. A caller rollback therefore consumes no ``k``.

Identity: ``(birth_uuid, mint_epoch, G, k)`` (DES-1); ``mint_epoch`` is the
epoch in force at PUBLICATION time (DES-2); ``k`` is a u64 per-(mint_epoch, G)
sequence from 0 (DES-4; first mint allocates 0). Retirement is fence-level
mint-retirement with row RETENTION (D4): epoch advance marks superseded-epoch
rows RETIRED in the same transaction; rows are never deleted here (OWN-01).

Host bound: SQLite INTEGER is signed 64-bit, so the u64 range above
``SQLITE_INT64_MAX`` is unrepresentable in ``k_next``/``epoch`` integer
storage. Both boundaries fail CLOSED with explicit errors (no wrap, no
silent reuse): values past u64 max raise from the u64 check; values whose
successor would exceed the host integer raise from the host check. The
conservative direction (refuse a mint the host cannot durably record) is
required by DUR-1/D-R8.1.

Single-writer assumption (DES-11/P1): the caller serializes publication
transactions (e.g. holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE). Primitives acquire no locks.
Contract violation (overlapping writers) surfaces LOUDLY, never as silent
duplicate allocation: a lost k-race raises ``StaleEpoch`` (retry in a new
txn), a lost first-mint race raises raw ``sqlite3.IntegrityError``.

classes.name: MintError
classes.doc: Base class for fail-closed mint authority errors.

classes.name: MintNotInitialized
classes.doc: No ``mint_epoch`` row: no epoch authority (DUR-4). Call ``init_mint``.

classes.name: StaleEpoch
classes.doc:
(birth, epoch) expectation does not match the fenced row (DUR-4/D-R1.4,
FAIL-5), or an ``advance_epoch`` CAS lost (U-2) — abort, no effects.

classes.name: RetiredCounter
classes.doc: The ``(mint_epoch, G)`` row is RETIRED: mint refused, no resurrection.

classes.name: CounterExhausted
classes.doc:
No further ``k`` allocatable for this ``(mint_epoch, G)`` (DES-10,
FAIL-1): u64 ceiling or host-integer ceiling reached. No wrap.

classes.name: EpochExhausted
classes.doc: Epoch cannot advance (DES-9, FAIL-2/F7.2 class): fail closed, no commits.

functions.name: init_mint
functions.doc:
Create the epoch-0 row if absent; return the fenced epoch.

Idempotent for the same ``birth_uuid`` (clean-restart path C-2/C-3: no
bump, counters untouched). A different birth against an initialized row
is rejected (FAIL-5). Never commits.

functions.name: mint
functions.doc:
Mint ``(mint_epoch, k)`` for ``generation_id`` in the caller's txn.

First read is the fenced ``(birth_uuid, epoch)`` row (DUR-4/D-R1.4);
absent row or expectation mismatch aborts with no effects. Then get (or
create at k=0) the LIVE row for ``(fenced_epoch, generation_id)``.
Never commits.

functions.name: advance_epoch
functions.doc:
Bump the fenced epoch by one (unclean-restart path U-2/O4) via CAS.

Compare-and-swap on ``expected_epoch`` (rowcount-checked: a lost race or
stale expectation raises ``StaleEpoch`` with no effects), then fence-mark
the superseded epoch's LIVE rows RETIRED — same transaction, rows
RETAINED, never deleted (D4). Returns the new epoch. Never commits.

functions.name: counter_row_count
functions.doc:
Total ``mint_counter`` rows (LIVE + retained RETIRED) for D4
backpressure accounting. Read-only; never commits.

module_doc:
Durable projection outbox (R01 migration 001).

Jobs are enqueued inside the source-replacement writer transaction and consumed
by workers OUTSIDE any writer transaction: claim -> work -> complete/fail.

Lease rules: ``lease_seconds`` minimum is 30 s (packet C1-3 limit). A claim picks
the oldest row that is ``pending`` or whose ``claimed`` lease has expired, so a
dead worker's job is reclaimable and a restarted process resumes from persisted
rows. Completion is idempotent: completing an already-``done`` job is a no-op
success. All methods take an explicit connection and never commit; the caller
owns the transaction boundary (single-statement calls commit immediately so a
crash between worker steps cannot lose state).

classes.name: LeaseError
classes.doc: Raised when a job is owned by a live lease held by another worker.

classes.name: JobStateError
classes.doc: Raised when an operation does not apply to the job's current state.

functions.name: enqueue
functions.doc: Enqueue a projection job; same idempotency key returns the existing job id.

functions.name: claim
functions.doc: Claim the oldest available job. Returns None when no job is claimable.

functions.name: complete
functions.doc: Mark a claimed job done. Idempotent: an already-done job returns True.

functions.name: fail
functions.doc: Return a claimed job to pending with its error recorded for retry.

functions.name: _parse_created
functions.doc: Parse an ISO-8601 ``created_at`` value to epoch seconds (None if bad).

functions.name: queue_stats
functions.doc:
Bounded queue measurement: depth, oldest-job lag, attempts, errors.

``depth`` is pending + claimed (all unfinished work). ``queue_lag_s``
is the age of the oldest unfinished job (None when the queue is
empty) — the backlog-lag metric S3/B1 require. All reads are small
aggregates over the outbox table; no projection or source rows are
touched.

functions.name: job_progress
functions.doc: Writer-progress counts by job state (done/total included).

functions.name: retry_delay_s
functions.doc:
Exponential backoff for a job (or batch) at 1-based ``attempt``.

Pure function: ``base * 2**(attempt-1)`` capped at ``cap_s``. The
worker sleeps this between retries; durability of the delay itself
is intentionally in-memory (a restart retries immediately, which is
always safe because every stage is idempotent).

functions.name: pressure_status
functions.doc:
Backpressure signal: pressured when unfinished depth >= watermark.

A pressured worker keeps draining bounded batches (reads are never
blocked) but reports pressure so supervisors can slow intake. The
watermark is caller-chosen; S4 owns tuning it.

module_doc:
Clean-shutdown marker detector (AMB-N06-6, N06b C-1/RST/U/C).

Sidecar-file mechanism: ``<db-path>.mint-shutdown`` (JSON, checksummed).
DB row is the authority (DUR-4); the marker is a hint only. Any
absent/torn/unverifiable marker fails CLOSED to the unclean path (C-1):
the caller bumps (read-current-write-plus-1, U-2), never fabricates.

Discipline (full argument: build/designs/N06/DETECTOR.md):
- Clean ``Database.close()`` writes the marker atomically
  (tmp + fsync + os.replace + fsync dir) binding (birth, epoch).
- ``Database.recover_mint()`` checks the marker against the fenced row,
  then INVALIDATES it (unlink) before serving, so a crash after open but
  before the next clean close leaves absent => unclean.
- Torn content (truncate/garbage/bad checksum), version/flag/field errors,
  or birth/epoch mismatch vs the fenced row => unclean, never clean.

Single-writer assumption (DES-11/P1): callers serialize opens/recovers;
concurrent openers racing marker unlink/write get at worst an extra
fail-closed bump, never silent reuse (CAS in ``mint.advance_epoch``).

functions.name: marker_path_for
functions.doc: Sidecar marker path for a database file path.

functions.name: compute_checksum
functions.doc: Hex checksum binding (birth, epoch) to the marker (torn-write detector).

functions.name: write_clean_marker
functions.doc:
Atomically write a valid clean-shutdown marker (clean-close path).

Raises ``ValueError`` for bad arguments, ``OSError`` for I/O failure
(caller decides: ``Database.close`` swallows I/O failure fail-closed —
absent marker => next open takes the unclean path with an extra bump).

functions.name: check_clean_marker
functions.doc:
Verify the marker against the fenced (birth, epoch).

Returns ``(is_clean, reason)``; ``reason`` is ``"clean"`` iff clean,
else one of ``absent``/``read-error``/``json-error``/``version-mismatch``/
``clean-flag``/``field-error``/``checksum``/``birth-mismatch``/
``epoch-mismatch``. Never raises for torn content (fail-closed False).

functions.name: invalidate_marker
functions.doc:
Remove the marker (open-path invalidation + crash-close simulation).

Missing marker is a no-op. I/O errors are swallowed: a stale marker left
behind mismatches the (possibly bumped) fenced epoch on the next open and
fails closed to unclean (extra bump, never reuse).
